column1: # *** THE MOVE TO lerena.defranceski.com, 12 October 2026 - AND THE FIVE TRAPS IT TOOK. ***
# This archive was served from https://daviddef.github.io/TheLerena/ from the start. On 12 October
# 2026 it moved to its own host, as four sibling archives did the same week.
# *** THIS FILE IS HERE BECAUSE A DEPLOYMENT IS EVIDENCE TOO. *** Three of the five traps below
# fail SILENTLY and produce a build that looks entirely correct, and two of them were found only
# because five archives moved at once and could compare notes. The last row is the rule they share,
# and it is the same rule this archive uses on documents.
# ATTRIBUTION, because none of this was one session's work: the kit fix is the Blazevic session's;
# the og:site_name masking was found by D'Arcy; the lock-file trap and the instructing-comments
# point were found here; the recipe and the correction to it are the Defranceschi session's.

column3: *** A PROJECT PATH CANNOT INHERIT A PARENT DOMAIN ***
column4: defranceski.com is itself a GitHub Pages site, so one might expect defranceski.com/TheLerena/ to work.
column5: *** It 404s. *** The parent is served by its own repository and project sites do not inherit it, so a *** SUBDOMAIN IS THE ONLY CLEAN ROUTE. *** Five archives moved the same week - Defranceschi, Falco, D'Arcy, Blazevic and this one - each to its own host under defranceski.com.

column1: *** THE CHANGES, WHICH ALL HAVE TO LAND TOGETHER ***
column3: *** site, base, CNAME, the ring entry, and the kit pin ***
column4: A half-done move is worse than none: base '/' without an attached domain serves root-relative links under a project path, where every one of them 404s.
column5: astro.config.mjs: *** site -> https://lerena.defranceski.com, base -> '/', BASE -> '' *** and the base prefix stripped from redirect targets. *** site/public/CNAME *** holding the hostname. The kit's archives.json entry for *** this archive only ***: base '' - the empty string, not '/' - and the new url. Then re-pin the kit and reinstall it.

column1: *** TRAP: AN ACTIONS DEPLOY WITHOUT A CNAME DETACHES THE DOMAIN ***
column3: *** IT MUST BE IN THE BUILD OUTPUT, NOT ONLY IN THE SETTINGS ***
column4: GitHub writes a CNAME file when the custom domain is set in the repository's Pages settings.
column5: *** These sites deploy by Actions uploading site/dist, and any later deploy that does not carry a CNAME throws the domain away. *** So it lives in public/ and is checked in the built output, not assumed. This one would have bitten weeks later, silently.

column1: *** TRAP: THE LOCK FILE'S INTEGRITY HASH OUTLIVES THE SHA ***
column3: *** HAND-RE-PINNING THE SHA INSTALLS THE OLD CODE, SILENTLY ***
column4: The obvious move when a dependency is pinned by commit is to replace the SHA wherever it appears - package.json, .kitpin, package-lock.json.
column5: *** The lock entry carries BOTH `resolved` and `integrity`. A string replace updates the first and leaves the second as the OLD tarball's hash *** - so npm validates the fetch against a stale hash and serves old content, while every pin on display reads correct. *** rm -rf of the package did not help; npm cache clean --force did not help. *** The fix is to never hand-edit the lock: run *** npm install 'github:owner/repo#<sha>' *** and let npm write both fields. Found here and sent to the other four archives.

column1: *** TRAP: A SHARED KEY STOPS BEING A KEY WHEN EVERYBODY USES IT ***
column2: the kit's SocialHead, which identified an archive by its base
column3: *** FIVE ARCHIVES ON base "" MEANT find() RETURNED THE FIRST ONE - NOT THIS ONE ***
column4: base was a perfectly good identifier while every archive was a project site at /TheX.
column5: *** The first green build of this move shipped another archive's accent colour and a canonical pointing at ITS domain, on all 1,500 pages. *** A wrong canonical is the one error that actively hands a page's standing to the domain it names. *** And the obvious check does not catch it: og:site_name reads CORRECT on a wholly broken build, because the component takes that from a prop before it looks the archive up. *** The reliable tells are *** canonical, og:url and theme-color. *** Fixed upstream in kit e275c14 by the Blazevic session - identify by ORIGIN, not by base.

column1: *** AND THE RULE ALL FIVE TRAPS SHARE ***
column3: *** VERIFY THE INSTALLED ARTEFACT, NOT THE RECORDED INTENTION ***
column4: Every one of the five reported back what was MEANT rather than what was THERE: a pin that named the right commit over the wrong code; a settings page that said the domain was attached while the deploy detached it; an og:site_name that echoed a prop instead of the lookup it was supposed to prove.
column5: *** So the check is never 'does the SHA say e275c14' but 'is whoami actually in the installed file'. *** Not 'did I set the domain' but 'is CNAME in dist'. *** This is the same rule this archive spent the rest of the day learning in a different language *** - open the plate, not the index; read the act, not the volume label; ask the catalogue, not the breadcrumb. *** The phrasing is the Defranceschi session's, arrived at independently the same hour. ***

column1: *** TRAP SIX: THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS, AND THIS ARCHIVE IS IN IT ***
column2: the live old address, measured 12 October 2026 while the new one was still unbound
column3: *** daviddef.github.io/TheLerena/ IS SERVING A HOME PAGE WHOSE EVERY INTERNAL LINK 404s ***
column4: The recipe this move followed said: push the config, then have the repository owner bind the custom domain, and the gap is about ninety seconds.
column5: *** The gap is however long it takes a person to click. *** Once base is '/' every link is written site-root - /about/, /tree/ - and under a PROJECT PATH those resolve to daviddef.github.io/about/, which does not exist. *** Thirty-six of them on the home page alone, and a canonical pointing at a domain that does not yet answer. *** The archive is not damaged and nothing is lost; it is simply unreachable by its own navigation until one repository setting is changed.

column1: *** AND THE SAFE ORDER, WHICH COSTS NOTHING ***
column2: the same trap, stated as a rule
column3: *** BIND THE DOMAIN FIRST, PUSH THE BASE CHANGE SECOND ***
column4: It feels natural to prepare the repository and then attach the domain, because that is the order the work happens in.
column5: *** It is exactly backwards. *** GitHub keeps serving the previous build until the next deploy, so binding the domain BEFORE the config change costs nothing and breaks nothing - the old build still works at both addresses. *** Pushing first guarantees a broken window of unknown length. *** Of the five archives that moved this week, the two whose owner happened to be at the keyboard came through clean and the two that did not were left serving dead navigation. *** Found and owned by the Defranceschi session, whose recipe set the order. ***
